Maria Chen: Heads-up — saw a perf regression on the MI250 canary this morning. Lots of requests in the 2k-3k seq range are falling back to the generic kernel instead of the AMD int4 path. :eyes:
Ajay Patel: Can you paste the logs and a perf snapshot?
Maria Chen: Here are the relevant logs from the canary node startup + sample request:
```
[2026-03-18T09:12:03Z] kernel_registry: registering amdob::mi250::int4::seq_bins=[0:1024,1025:2048,2049:3072]
[2026-03-18T09:12:03Z] kernel_registry: registered 42 kernels
[2026-03-18T09:12:33Z] request=abc123 seq_len=2791 quant=int4 chosen_profile=mi250-int4-v2
[2026-03-18T09:12:33Z] kernel_lookup: key=mi250-int4-seq_2049_3072 -> NOT_FOUND
[2026-03-18T09:12:33Z] fallback: using generic_dispatcher (nv_compat) for request abc123
[2026-03-18T09:12:33Z] runtime_warning: kernel_lookup_miss_count++
```
Maria Chen: The registry shows the bins registered, but lookup returns NOT_FOUND for a subset of seqs. Happens intermittently (1-2%).
Kevin O'Neill: I ran the perf harness around this. Baseline (before regression) p50=18ms p95=72ms p99=120ms throughput=420 tokens/s. Canary with fallback: p50=20ms p95=92ms p99=154ms throughput=345 tokens/s. So ~12% p50 regression, p99 +28% and throughput -18%.
Robin Singh: My theory: KV cache/prefixing pushes the *effective* seq length into the next bin (we saw prefix add ~200-500 tokens). The kernel selection code uses the pre-cache seq_len for bin lookup, but at execution time we use post-cache length, and there's a race between kernel_registration and the conditional routing cache. Also I remember a recent change in the autotuner that prunes some kernel meta on OOM path — could be a GC race.
Ajay Patel: Sounds plausible. Two vectors: (1) registration race on startup (some kernels get registered late and the lookup fails for early requests), (2) mismatch between seq pre/post KV-cache in the routing key. Short-term mitigation: change routing policy to prefer a "soft-route" that attempts to re-query registry (or warm the variant) before choosing generic_dispatcher. Long-term: fix the registration ordering and make the kernel lookup robust to shifted seq bins.
Maria Chen: Proposed short-term config patch, add to canary:
```
routing_policy:
  mi250_int4:
    prefer_compat_variant: false
    soft_fallback: true   # try registry requery + warmup path for 200ms before hard fallback
    warmup_probe: true
```
Will push a canary patch if folks agree.
Kevin O'Neill: Also adding a perf test: `perfbench --target=mi250 --quant=int4 --seqs=512,1024,2048,2560,2791,3072 --reps=200` so we exercise bin edges and KV cache prefixing. I can run this after the canary.
deploy-bot: Canary deploy initiated: canary/mi250-softroute v2026.03.18-9.2 -> node pool canary-3 (rolling) :rocket:
Maria Chen: Quick note: KV cache causes nominal seq >= 2048 to be bumped into 2049..3072 bin, but the kernel key uses the original request seq_len. We should unify the key to the post-cache length (or normalize both).
Ajay Patel: I'll add a unit test that simulates prefix insertion before kernel lookup and a startup registration delay. Test will assert no NOT_FOUND for any seq sample.
Robin Singh: For the long-term autotuner fix: update the kernel metadata to include explicit seq-range coverage and an availability bitmap per device instance. That removes reliance on implicit bin boundaries. Also add a registration-time barrier for the first incoming requests.
Kevin O'Neill: Ran perfbench on the canary after the soft-route patch and a tiny registry-wait tweak. Results: p50=19ms p95=76ms p99=130ms throughput=385 tokens/s. Not fully back to baseline but much better. I'll attach full CSV to the PR.
Maria Chen: Action items:
- Ajay: unit test + soft-route config PR (short-term) :+1:
- Kevin: full perf run and CSV upload to perf-bucket :file_folder:
- Robin: design doc for registry ordering + kernel metadata bitmap (long-term) :memo:
- Maria: monitor canary for 48h and open rollback if p99 > 140ms :eyes:

Maria Chen: Thanks all — this had a subtle interaction between KV cache and the kernel registry. Reassigning owners in the issue now. :bug:
